why: a `;` in a string literal ends nothing

an E that ends a word is no escape-string prefix

why: a tagged body ends only at its own tag

why: a `$` inside a word is part of the word, no dollar quote

why: a `;` in a line comment ends nothing
a `;` in a block comment ends nothing

statements: SELECT 1 /* outer /* inner */ still a comment; */ + 1

why: the comments around a statement are not part of it
text that is only comments is no statement
an empty statement is none

SELECT a+-- x; y

why: the last statement needs no `;`
a rule's actions are statements inside parentheses

statements: CREATE RULE r AS ON INSERT TO t DO ALSO (INSERT INTO a VALUES (1); INSERT INTO b VALUES (2))

why: a SQL-standard routine body runs from BEGIN ATOMIC to its END, CASE ... END inside it

statements: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION f() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql BEGIN ATOMIC SELECT CASE WHEN true THEN 1 END; SELECT 2; END

why: and a procedure's, in any case

why: outside a routine, BEGIN and END are a transaction's
